description: We are a team of three passionate beginners interested in space exploration, science, and creativity. We aim to create an engaging and educational project that tells the stories of forgotten space exploration equipment and inspires young people to discover the wonders of space.
summary:
Two rovers were built to last 90 days. One worked for 14 years. Both went silent, and the world called them abandoned. We tell the story they never got to tell.

Pico: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive web story narrated by Pico, a tiny red Lego piece that rides to Mars for good luck. Pico meets Spirit in Gusev Crater and Opportunity on the other side of the planet, and hears how they found clues that water once shaped Mars and outlived their plans by about 25 and nearly 60 times.

The story comes with science anyone can explore: a tap-to-explore rover anatomy, a 2003-2019 timeline, a planned vs. real mission length chart, a quiz, and other machines like Sojourner, Viking, Phoenix, InSight and Ingenuity.

Our message: a rover's wheels may stop, but its data keeps teaching. Spirit and Opportunity's findings remain open to everyone in NASA's Planetary Data System.

Facts: NASA/JPL mission pages. Images: NASA public domain.
details:
What it does: Pico is an interactive web story about NASA's retired Mars rovers Spirit and Opportunity, told by Pico, a small red Lego piece that travels to Mars. Readers follow Pico to Gusev Crater and the other side of the planet, then explore the science behind the story.

Benefits and intended impact: Rover missions are usually told through numbers. Our project turns them into a character-driven journey that students and curious readers of any age can follow, and shows that "abandoned" machines are not forgotten: their data is still open to everyone in NASA's Planetary Data System.

What is inside: a tap-to-explore rover anatomy, a 2003-2019 mission timeline, a planned vs. real mission length comparison, a quiz, and other machines Pico could meet (Sojourner, Viking, Phoenix, InSight, Ingenuity).

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single web page, hosted on tiiny.host. Facts come from NASA/JPL Mars Exploration Rover mission pages and news releases. Photos are NASA/JPL-Caltech/Cornell public-domain images. Pico is an original graphic.

Creativity: we told a hardware story through the eyes of the smallest object on the spacecraft. Our team name, Red Echo, means the Red Planet and an echo: something that continues after the original sound has faded.

Factors we considered: scientific accuracy, accessibility for all ages, correct credit for NASA images, and keeping the story short enough to read in one sitting.
